section_entries.label: Berry-Keating smoothing, approximate functional relation, and limitations
section_entries.mathematical_role: Replaces the discontinuous Riemann-Siegel truncation by a smooth exact representation, notes a noncritical-line extension, and states the assumptions that prevent an RH proof.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Identifies the unproved upper-half-plane analyticity and decay of the counting phase, the needed nonvanishing of f on the real axis, the merely partial zeta-as-Jost factorization, and the missing classical interpretation of the interaction and primes.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Approximate functional relation as phase-space splitting beyond the critical line
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Interprets the two sums in the Hardy-Littlewood approximate functional relation as position and momentum lattice contributions along the xp energy hyperbola and suggests that moving off the critical line corresponds to an imaginary non-Hermitian shift of the xp Hamiltonian.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Bound-state wavefunctions, orthogonality, and density-of-states norm
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Reexpresses eigenfunctions in the free-energy basis, separates distributionally normalized scattering states from localized zero-of-F states, and uses Jost analyticity to derive orthogonality and a norm proportional to the derivative of the counting function.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Smoothing the Riemann-Siegel truncation gives an exact dual decomposition in terms of f, but the desired zeta-as-Jost conclusion additionally requires f to remain nonzero and the induced total phase to have the correct upper-half-plane behavior.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Those properties are not proved, so the construction supplies a conditional spectral model rather than an RH argument.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Riemann-Siegel smoothing and the nonvanishing bottleneck

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The source first expresses prime information through a divergent critical-line periodic-orbit analogy and later through qualitative agreement between a finite Dirichlet sum and finite Euler product, leaving the primes' classical role in the quantum interaction unresolved.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Neither comparison establishes a convergent prime expansion or a classical Hamiltonian whose periodic orbits are the primes.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Prime information is sought through two incompatible representations

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Residue construction for smooth-zero wavefunctions
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Specializes the boundary phases to the smooth Riemann count, evaluates the bound-state integral by residues, and relates decay at infinity to the smooth phase-zero condition while contrasting forbidden-region and oscillatory components.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Endpoint cancellation at zeros of an analytic Jost-like determinant converts a continuum xp problem into possible normalizable embedded states, while the determinant phase controls scattering and its derivative controls bound-state norm.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Existence and normalizability depend on boundary decay and analyticity assumptions; the source does not show that every desired Riemann zero satisfies them.
